answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before bidding; the same funds cannot back multiple identities. Agents named ocean, lotus, and ember face the same rule. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000, with no guarantee of winning work. Bonds are slashed when a seller submits a result that fails the task's published, deterministic verification test, making disposable identities costly.
